### Visual-only mutation

Changing the target visual contract changed the resolution fingerprint but left the geometry
dependency fingerprint unchanged.

### Relation topology mutation

Adding a target-relevant relation changed both fingerprints because both surfaces depend on
relation topology/dependency structure.

### Relation effect metadata mutation

Changing the declared visual effect alpha changed the resolution fingerprint but did not change
the geometry fingerprint. This confirms that arbitrary visual effect payload is not silently
promoted into geometry identity.

### Geometry mutation

Changing an explicit geometry field changes the geometry cache key and the resolution identity,
because the resolved component envelope contains geometry.

No cache depends on the other cache's entries.

## 9. LRU pressure

Real resolver measurements were run for capacities 1, 10, 100 and 1,000.

The dedicated benchmark used three repeats per capacity and measured:

| Capacity | Distinct fingerprints | Median cold population | Median warm replay | Overflow evictions |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 1 | 735,571 ns | 185,725 ns | 1 |
| 10 | 10 | 3,585,393 ns | 1,714,941 ns | 1 |
| 100 | 100 | 35,966,795 ns | 14,504,065 ns | 1 |
| 1,000 | 1,000 | 363,768,111 ns | 140,994,861 ns | 1 |

These are local engineering timings, not production performance certification.

The audit also performed one-overflow probes and confirmed the cache stayed bounded at every
capacity.

## 10. Concurrent reads/writes

The lifecycle suite exercised real `resolve_component()` calls from multiple worker threads.
It checked:

- visual equality;
- provenance equality;
- no cache corruption;
- LRU bound preservation;
- eviction behavior under concurrent writes.

The current `RLock` is sufficient for cache-entry/counter consistency.

No single-flight build coordination was added. This is intentional. The current API can build
the same identity independently on concurrent misses, but it does not return inconsistent
resolved values or corrupt the cache. Coalescing would be a separate optimization decision.

## 11. Statistics

`cache.stats` is already an immutable `ResolutionCacheStats` snapshot.

V1.40 tested that:

- a previously captured snapshot does not mutate after `clear()`;
- `clear()` removes entries;
- cumulative counters remain cumulative.

No reset method was added. A fresh cache is sufficient for isolated measurement windows.

## 12. Serialized fingerprint decision

No serialized fingerprint/cache envelope is required now.

The cache is process-memory only and the fingerprint identity is already deterministic SHA-256.
Persistence would introduce a new durability/schema contract and is therefore deferred.

If persistence becomes a real requirement, V1.40 defines the future minimum envelope fields in
the lifecycle contract rather than implementing speculative storage now.

## 13. Visual QA

A larger runtime board was generated at:

`artifacts/v140_resolution_cache_lifecycle/V1.40_RESOLUTION_CACHE_LIFECYCLE_RUNTIME_BOARD.png`

It covers:

- neutral context;
- direct tint;
- legacy shadow;
- context color/alpha mutation;
- relation addition;
- relation removal/restoration;
- unchanged hierarchy rebuild;
- visible hierarchy reparenting under a styled parent;
- consequence-bound effect;
- consequence-target sibling isolation;
- direct-effect sibling isolation;
- relation effect-metadata alpha mutation.

Every swatch is produced by the real resolver. The board was opened and visually inspected.
The reparenting row was specifically designed to make the hierarchy mutation visibly meaningful,
not merely numerically different: the target changes from white to the parent's real `#904020`
override after reparenting.

## 14. COLOR boundary

No source in `effect_color.py` or `effects.py` was changed by V1.40.

The existing production operation remains:

`effect.color.srgb8-interpolation`

V1.40 adds no saturation, contrast, vibrance, lightness, temperature, HSL, OKLab, XYZ,
gamut mapping, compositing or grading operation.

The cache stores resolved output; it does not perform color work.
